title: Evaluation at one on homotopy classes of structure-sheaf maps
statement: Let X be a ringed space, C the category of sheaves of O_X-modules, A=Gamma(X,O_X), and G:K(C) to K(A) the termwise global-sections functor [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. Cochain complexes are as in [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], and K is their category modulo chain homotopy. Let P be O_X in degree zero and Q be the free rank-one A-module in degree zero, viewed in these homotopy categories. There exists a family of additive equivalences e_J:Hom_K(C)(P,J) equiv+ Hom_K(A)(Q,GJ), natural in every homotopy-category morphism: e_Jprime(g composed with f)=e_J(g) composed with G(f). No boundedness, acyclicity, injectivity, quasi-coherence or topological finiteness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Proposition perfect-proposition-compact-is-perfect (Tag 09M1), proof, first paragraph, structure-sheaf specialization; evaluation-at-one calculation expanded from parent proof step 2; Tag 0B6A

proof.text: For every module sheaf M, termwise global sections induces a bijection from Hom(O_X,M) to Hom_A(A,Gamma(X,M)). For injectivity, use SheafOfModules.unitHomEquiv and naturality along the restriction from the total open to U: evaluation at one on U is the restriction of evaluation at one on X. For surjectivity, restrict the value at one of an A-linear map on the total open to every U, obtaining a compatible family of sections, and apply unitHomEquiv.symm. LinearMap.ext_ring verifies the inverse at one. This proves the private helper unit_evaluation_bijective; no exactness or injectivity property is used.

Put K=O_X[0]. The degree-zero component is isomorphic to O_X by singleObjXSelf, so the bijection of step 1 transports to maps from K.X 0. Every other component is zero by isZero_single_obj_X, and global sections preserves zero objects, so both Hom sets are singletons. Thus for every degree i and module sheaf Y, the global-sections map from Hom(K.X i,Y) to Hom(Gamma(K.X i),Gamma(Y)) is bijective.

For any additive functor F and complex K satisfying the termwise bijectivity of step 2, lift a chain map FK to FL by applying the inverse Hom bijection to each component. Applying F to the desired chain-map equation gives the original equation; injectivity verifies it. Likewise lift every component of a homotopy between two image chain maps: applying F verifies the vanishing conditions and the homotopy equation, since F preserves zero, addition and composition. Fullness of the homotopy quotient gives chain-map representatives. homotopyOfEq turns equality of their images into a homotopy; the lifted homotopy and eq_of_homotopy prove injectivity. Lifting a representative proves surjectivity. These constructions are the fully proved private helper map_homotopy_bijective.

The singleMapHomologicalComplex isomorphism identifies the termwise global sections of K with A[0], since evaluating the unit at the total open is exactly the free rank-one A-module. Apply the homotopy quotient to obtain a:G(P) isomorphic to Q. Define e_J(g)=a.inv composed with G(g). Step 3 proves bijectivity, and additivity of G and composition gives AddEquiv.ofBijective. Finally e_Jprime(g composed with f)=e_J(g) composed with G(f) follows from Functor.map_comp and associativity. This applies equally to empty ringed spaces, the zero ring, and unbounded complexes.

lean.statement:
theorem structureSheaf_homotopy_globalSections (X : RingedSpace.{u}) :
    let C := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X)
    let A := (moduleRings X).obj.obj (op ⊤)
    let P := (HomotopyCategory.quotient C (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj
      ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor C 0).obj
        (SheafOfModules.unit (moduleRings X)))
    let Q := (HomotopyCategory.quotient (ModuleCat.{u} A) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj
      ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj (ModuleCat.of A A))
    let G := (RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X).mapHomotopyCategory
      (ComplexShape.up ℤ)
    ∃ e : ∀ J : HomotopyCategory C (ComplexShape.up ℤ),
      (P ⟶ J) ≃+ (Q ⟶ G.obj J),
      ∀ (J J' : HomotopyCategory C (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) (f : J ⟶ J') (g : P ⟶ J),
        e J' (g ≫ f) = e J g ≫ G.map f
